evidence.claim: A winding county road links hamlets through a succession of right-angle turns.
evidence.quote: SR 14 heads southeast as The Trail, a winding highway with multiple right-angle turns that serves as the primary north–south highway of King and Queen County.

evidence.claim: The Trail is Route 14’s winding run southeast from US 360 at St. Stephens Church through King and Queen County.
evidence.quote: SR 14 begins at an intersection with US 360 (Richmond–Tappahannock Highway) in St. Stephens Church.

evidence.claim: Multiple right-angle turns shape the drive along the county’s main north–south highway.
evidence.quote: SR 14 heads southeast as The Trail, a winding highway with multiple right-angle turns that serves as the primary north–south highway of King and Queen County.

evidence.claim: It passes hamlets and the county seat before meeting Route 33 at Shacklefords.
evidence.quote: SR 14 continues southeast through the small communities of Truhart, Little Plymouth, Shanghai, and Elsom to its junction with SR 33 (Lewis Puller Memorial Highway) in Shacklefords.

evidence.claim: The Route 14 number once continued northwest beyond St. Stephens Church toward Bowling Green; that older alignment is now Route 721, Newtown Road.
evidence.quote: The roadway continues on the north side of the intersection as SR 721 (Newtown Road), the old route of SR 14 that continues northwest to near Bowling Green.

evidence.claim: The numbered highway now starts at US 360 and connects the county seats of King and Queen, Gloucester and Mathews counties.
evidence.quote: SR 14 is the primary highway of King and Queen and Mathews counties and the main east–west highway of Gloucester County; the highway connects the namesake county seats of all three counties.

evidence.claim: From St. Stephens Church, follow The Trail southeast through Bruington and Stevensville to King and Queen Court House.
evidence.quote: The state highway passes through the hamlets of Bruington, Henleys Fork, Stevensville, Cumnor on its way to the county seat of King and Queen Court House

evidence.claim: The county seat lies on the north side of the Mattaponi River valley.

evidence.claim: Beyond it come Little Plymouth, Shanghai and Elsom, then the junction with Route 33 at Shacklefords.

evidence.claim: Near Stevensville, the junction of Routes 631 and 632 has been known as Dahlgrens Corner since at least 1918.
evidence.quote: near Stevensville at a junction known as Dahlgrens Corner since at least 1918. It is at the intersection of Virginia State Route 631 and Virginia State Route 632.

evidence.claim: The name recalls Union colonel Ulric Dahlgren, killed in King and Queen County in March 1864 after his force failed to penetrate Richmond’s defenses.
evidence.quote: Meanwhile, Dahlgren had found himself unable to penetrate Richmond's defenses, and tried to escape northwards.

evidence.claim: Confederate cavalry and Home Guards ambushed his group near Walkerton; most survivors were captured.
evidence.quote: Dahlgren, along with about 100 men, was ambushed by a detachment of the 9th Virginia Cavalry and Home Guards in King and Queen County near Walkerton. Dahlgren was killed with several of his men and most of the rest were captured.

evidence.claim: Papers found on his body allegedly ordered Richmond burned and Jefferson Davis and his cabinet assassinated.
evidence.quote: The papers allegedly contained an official Union order to burn Richmond and assassinate Jefferson Davis and his cabinet.

evidence.claim: Their authenticity is disputed; Meade, Kilpatrick and Lincoln disavowed knowledge of them.
evidence.quote: Meade, Kilpatrick, and Lincoln all disavowed any knowledge of the Dahlgren Papers, and their authenticity has been disputed.

flags: Designation evidence gap: 01.txt omits the byway table and 00.txt does not identify this segment as a Virginia Byway. The catalog designation, March 21, 2002 date and agency rationale cannot be re-established from cache; omitted from public text. This remains an editorial hold.

Road history is limited to the former Route 14 alignment now numbered 721; no date, builder, original purpose or explanation of the name The Trail is cached. Overview is shorter than target; no terrain detail or drive time is invented.

Corrected current Stevensville claim that Dahlgren was killed during an assassination attempt: 08.txt explicitly disputes the authenticity of the alleged orders, whereas 02.txt states the attempt without qualification. No primary account is cached.

Upper Church is deliberately short because 15.txt offers only a compact architectural and restoration account. It describes Episcopal origins and Baptist/Methodist use without confirming present denomination or visitor access; no visiting arrangements are asserted.

The current Shacklefords family-name history and courthouse population are supported, but omitted for focus. The current phrase the spelling has never quite settled overstates the evidence, which only documents variant spellings.
